test_title: PYST 13: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - GA (Held On 24 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: How is the data for the Happiness Index collected?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Through self-reported surveys**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The data for the **World Happiness Index** is primarily collected through **self-reported surveys** conducted by the **Gallup World Poll**. This poll samples approximately **1,000** individuals from nearly every country annually to assess their **subjective well-being**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The core of the survey is the **Cantril Ladder**, where respondents are asked to think of a ladder, with the best possible life for them being a **10** and the worst possible life being a **0**. They then rate their own current lives on that **0 to 10 scale**.
 
• The index does not rely on **satellite images** to determine happiness, as these are typically used for environmental or geographical data rather than human emotion or life satisfaction. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• While **GDP per capita** is one of the six variables used to explain the variation in happiness across countries, the index is not calculated **by measuring GDP only**. It integrates socio-economic factors with individual perceptions. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The report does not determine rankings **by analyzing internet usage**. While digital data can provide insights into behavior, the formal **World Happiness Report** methodology relies on direct human responses regarding their quality of life. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The World Happiness Report (WHR)**: This is an annual publication by the **United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)**. It was first released in **2012** following the **UN High-Level Meeting** on "Happiness and Well-Being: Defining a New Economic Paradigm."
 
• **Six Key Variables**: To explain the differences in reported happiness levels, researchers analyze six factors: **GDP per capita**, **Social support** (having someone to count on), **Healthy life expectancy**, **Freedom to make life choices**, **Generosity** (donations to charity), and **Perceptions of corruption**.
 
• **Gross National Happiness (GNH)**: The concept of measuring happiness instead of just economic growth originated in **Bhutan**. In **1972**, the 4th King of Bhutan, **Jigme Singye Wangchuck**, declared that "Gross National Happiness is more important than Gross Domestic Product."
 
• **Top Performing Countries**: Nordic countries consistently dominate the top of the rankings. **Finland** has been ranked as the happiest country in the world for **seven consecutive years** as of the **2024** report. Other high-ranking nations include **Denmark**, **Iceland**, and **Sweden**.
 
• **India's Ranking**: In recent years, **India** has generally ranked lower on the index compared to many of its neighbors. In the **2024** report, India was ranked **126th** out of 143 countries surveyed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Release Date**: The report is typically released annually on **March 20th**, which is recognized by the **United Nations** as the **International Day of Happiness**.
 
• **Methodology Stability**: To ensure data reliability and reduce the impact of outliers or temporary events, the report uses a **three-year average** of the **Gallup World Poll** data for its final rankings.
 
• **Dystopia**: The report uses a hypothetical country called **Dystopia**, representing the lowest national averages for each of the six key variables. This serves as a **regression benchmark** to compare how much each factor contributes to a real country's happiness score.
 
• **Subjective vs. Objective**: The primary rank is strictly **subjective** (based on what people say), while the six variables used for explanation are **objective** (based on national statistics and survey data on specific behaviors).
